newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia region court seeks to block Tyumen Oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Russia region court seeks to block Tyumen Oil sale.

text.p: A regional Russian court has called for a forthcoming investment tender for 40 percent of the Tyumen Oil Company (TNK) to be cancelled, a TNK official said on Friday.

The official, from TNK's legal section, said an arbitration court in the Siberian city of Tyumen, where TNK is located, had urged that the sale be scrapped after a firm called Trans World Holding filed a suit seeking to block the tender.
The tender is due to be held July 16, with results to be announced two days later.
It was not immediately clear if a regional court could actually block a sale ordered by the federal government.
But First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko told Reuters in Salzburg he did not think a regional court could block the sale.

TNK, one of the last Russian oil companies to be privatised, is about 90 percent state-owned. Separately, a TNK source said that on Friday Trans World sold its nine percent stake in TNK to a Luxembourg-based company called Cadet Establishment.
The TNK tender, one of the last sell-offs of a major Russian oil company, has come under fire in recent weeks as company officials argue over the terms and desirability of the sale.
Russian officials said earlier this week the terms of the sale would be amended so that they were fair for all bidders.

The 40 percent TNK stake has a price tag of about $25 million for the stock and $160 million in investment over two years. In a separate sale, Russia is due to offer around 47 percent of TNK through special cash auctions starting August 5.

TNK's main production unit is Nizhnevartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS. TNK's 1996 production, which accounted for about seven percent of Russia's total oil output that year, fell six percent to 426,000 barrels per day.
